# The Headless Horse

The Headless Horse is Equestria's spooky **ghost-story horse** in *My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic* (G4). **Its on-screen appearance is confirmed** in “Sleepless in Ponyville” (S3E6): Scootaloo is pursued by its tall, very dark blue, mare-shaped silhouette, flowing indigo-edged tail, and visibly absent head. **What remains unconfirmed is its physical existence outside a dream**; the shown pursuit is Scootaloo's nightmare, not a waking encounter.

[![The Headless Horse rearing against the moon — *Sleepless in Ponyville* television still](https://cdn.twibooru.org/img/2020/7/20/1742588/medium.png)](https://twibooru.org/1742588)

*Image: production still from* Friendship Is Magic, *credited to the Hasbro television production; the linked archive post identifies the episode.*

**Name and continuity.** “The Headless Horse” is the **on-screen name**, not a fan nickname: Twilight introduces *The Legend of the Headless Horse* in “Look Before You Sleep” ([episode dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Look_Before_You_Sleep)). The licensed mobile game lists a character as simply **Headless Horse** and uses it as a boss helper ([game character record](https://mlp-gameloft.fandom.com/wiki/Headless_Horse)); that game depiction does not establish that the nightmare creature physically exists in the television story. The figure's mare-like design and a feminine reference in a guidebook explain its grouping with mares, although the show usually uses neutral language ([character overview](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/The_Headless_Horse)).

**Speaking and other appearances.** The Headless Horse **has no spoken dialogue or identified voice actor**. Beyond the S1 story and S3 nightmare, Rarity briefly considers a “headless pony” costume in “Scare Master” (S5E21; [episode transcript](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Scare_Master)). A book called *The Headless Horse* also appears in the IDW mini-comic *The Fall of Sunset Shimmer*. **Princess Luna is not a confirmed alternate identity**: Scootaloo mistakes Luna for the monster, and Luna corrects her ([dream dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Sleepless_in_Ponyville)). **The Olden Pony is a separate character**: the elderly mare seeking her rusty horseshoe speaks in Scootaloo's nightmares, including the final dream sequence. Her ending appearance should not be misidentified as the Headless Horse or treated as evidence that either ghost-story figure physically appeared while Scootaloo was awake ([episode transcript](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Sleepless_in_Ponyville); [Olden Pony character listing](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_ponies/Elders)).



## The Olden Pony in the ending (separate character)

The episode's final nightmare shows **the Olden Pony**, an elderly mare looking for her rusty horseshoe. Rainbow Dash gives it back, and Princess Luna chuckles. **This is not the Headless Horse**. The following identification image shows the Olden Pony from S3E6; the archive identifies the character, but the image is **not independently verified as a frame from the closing exchange**.

[![The Olden Pony — elderly mare from Sleepless in Ponyville (S3E6), not the Headless Horse](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/mlp/images/d/de/Olden_Pony_id_S3E6.png/revision/latest?cb=20121223085111)](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/File:Olden_Pony_id_S3E6.png)

*Image: Hasbro Studios television screenshot, indexed as “Olden Pony id S3E6.png”; [episode screenshot catalogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Sleepless_in_Ponyville_images). Image-host availability and local caching have not been independently verified.*

## Important moments

1. **Twilight's slumber-party scare — “Look Before You Sleep” (S1E8).** Twilight tells the legend to Rarity and Applejack, delivering its name as a jump scare; this establishes the Equestrian folklore. [Verified full episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oGck5MKWrKI) — exact scene timestamp unavailable.
2. **Rainbow's forest warning — “Sleepless in Ponyville” (S3E6).** Rainbow Dash describes the headless horse hunting lost ponies, terrifying Scootaloo despite Applejack's questions about its anatomy. [Verified full episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FkSzs6KERmU) — exact scene timestamp unavailable.
3. **The nightmare and Luna — “Sleepless in Ponyville” (S3E6).** Scootaloo is chased by the silhouette, but Luna's intervention reveals that her deeper fear is disappointing Rainbow Dash. [Episode account](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Sleepless_in_Ponyville) — exact scene timestamp unavailable.
4. **The “wicked whinny” — “Sleepless in Ponyville” (S3E6).** Mistaking Rainbow's snoring for the monster, Scootaloo runs into real danger; Rainbow rescues her, and their sister-like bond begins. Same verified full episode above; exact scene timestamp unavailable.
5. **The Olden Pony's return — “Sleepless in Ponyville” (S3E6), final dream sequence.** Scootaloo dreams again of the old mare demanding her missing rusty horseshoe. Rainbow returns it, and Luna laughs. This character is **the Olden Pony, not the Headless Horse**. [Episode transcript](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Sleepless_in_Ponyville).
appearance: Confirmed on screen as a tall, very dark blue headless equine silhouette with a flowing dark blue, indigo-edged tail in Scootaloo's dream in “Sleepless in Ponyville” (S3E6); no confirmed waking-world appearance.
speakingStatus: No confirmed spoken dialogue or voice actor; The Olden Pony's rusty-horseshoe dialogue belongs to a separate character.
